verified.todo_source:
# Keep track of what needs doing.
app Todos
Given
 Todo { title:text trim min=1 max=200 label="Task", done:bool=false label={text="Status",values={true="Done",false="Open"}} } label="Todo"
 policy Todo read=members
 fixture task=Todo {title="Try Can"}
When
 crud Todo by=members fields=title,done label={create="Add task"}
  examples update record=task
   as,changes.done,request.record.version -> record.done
   members,true,1 -> true
   members,true,0 -> error(conflict)
   public,true,1 -> error(forbidden)
Then
 preferences { view:enum(all,open,done)=all label={text="Show",values={all="All",open="Open",done="Done"}} }
 page / title="Todos"
  card "Add a task"
   form Todo.create fields=title display=inline
    input title
  card "Your tasks"
   tabs preferences.view
   list Todo as task where preferences.view==all or (preferences.view==open and not task.done) or (preferences.view==done and task.done) order=-created search=title empty="No tasks here. Add a task or choose another view."
    text row.title,row.done
    edit fields=title,done
    tooltip "Permanently delete this task"
     delete
verified.record_syntax: Existing Can records use comma-separated NAME=value members; nested records exist.
verified.current_styling: Then has finite producer-catalog component appearance and core card layout=stack|columns, but no generic per-component spacing/sizing/responsive styling. CSS acquisition currently uses prebuilt daisyUI plus manually supplied utilities. No proposed syntax is implemented.

state.context: Design stage only: the requested deliverable is a short way to author individual-component CSS and viewport overrides in Then, with a Todo source example. Every candidate is evaluated for identical layout, spacing, dimensions, completion/errors, concise composition and deterministic responsive behavior, not for already implemented compiler support. Can already accepts nested NAME=value records and finite component appearance choices; it lacks a general style surface. The standard shell still supplies the desktop left menu and small-screen drawer. Styling continues through existing canonical field access, CRUD defaults, CSRF/version checks and archive semantics.
state.shared_semantics: Use the same proposed semantic model for each candidate: pinned style aliases with property-specific value types, literal spacing scale values and validated length strings, compiler-emitted CSS, explicit catalog root/body/repeated-row targets and no unbounded descendant selectors. Defaults are refined by base values then matching sm40rem/md48rem/lg64rem/xl80rem rules in width order. Conflicting normalized properties within one rule are rejected, while responsive replacements are allowed. No candidate changes handlers, required generated controls or read authority.

syntax.instructions: For this finite draft, select the spelling that offers the strongest joint tradeoff across source size, reader comprehension, style/business separation, authoring diagnostics and viewport refinement.

criteria.map: Nest style declarations in css={p=4,gap=3,sm={p=6}}. Existing record syntax and a dedicated style namespace support structured tooling, at the cost of braces and separators; owned parts are nested entries.
criteria.attrs: Place p=4 gap=3 sm={p=6} beside ordinary component attributes. Less punctuation makes short styles brief; resolving style/behavior name collisions must be specified; parts are other direct entries.
criteria.string: Use css="p-4 gap-3 sm:p-6". A finite utility-token parser can validate this familiar concise representation and part prefixes, while tooling works within a string grammar.
criteria.defer: Offer no preferred candidate if the requirements still make all three unsuitable; retain the decision as open.
